The graph above shows $y={g}^{″}(x),$ where the function $g(x)$ is defined on $[-5,5].$ Find the intervals on which the function $g(x)$ is concave up.
worked_solution:
A function $g(x)$ is concave up over an interval $(a,b)$ if ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

On the given graph of $y={g}^{″}(x)$, we can see that ${g}^{″}(x)>0$ on the interval $(0,5)$ only. Therefore, the function $g(x)$ is concave up on the interval $(0,5)$ only.
